title: Saved templates silently drop the Overtime flag, so reusing one understates the shift's value with no on-screen signal
where: index.html:4140-4160 (doSaveTemplate builds `tpl` without isOvertime), :4135-4139 (applyTemplateTap never sets isOvertime on the shift it inserts), :2915-2926 (toggleQuickFillDay same), :1051-1068 (templates sanitizeData branch has no isOvertime field at all)
detail: The template object model has no isOvertime field anywhere in its lifecycle: doSaveTemplate's `tpl = {name, shiftType, hours, bonusType, customBonus, ...start}` (line 4154) never reads it, even though the same function goes out of its way (comment at 4144-4150) to correctly recover bonusType/customBonus/start from the just-added list entry so the template 'faithfully captures what's on the day.' Both places a template is turned back into a shift -- applyTemplateTap (4136) and quick-fill's toggleQuickFillDay (2922) -- construct the new shift object without an isOvertime key, so it's always falsy. The templates branch of sanitizeData (1051-1068) also has no isOvertime coercion, confirming this isn't a one-off omission but the actual data shape.
failure: A nurse configures Night 12h + Overtime + On-call bonus (base $40, night diff $10/hr -> $50/hr differential rate). The live preview correctly shows 1.5x972 + 60 = about $1,032 take-home-adjusted gross, she clicks '+ Add to this day', then immediately 'Save as template' (e.g. named 'Mandatory OT night'). Any later use of that template -- the one-tap 'QUICK ADD FROM TEMPLATE' chip in the sheet, or bulk quick-fill across days on the calendar -- adds a shift worth only base+diff x12 + bonus (about $708, 31% less), because isOvertime is silently false. Nothing in the UI discloses this: the per-shift row in 'ON THIS DAY' (4192-4202) shows no dollar figure at all, so there's nothing to contradict the number she remembers from when she built the template, and no toast/label ever says 'overtime not saved to templates.' This directly breaks the promise of knowing what a shift is worth before working it -- the number she believes she reproduced isn't the number she'll actually get.
fix: Include isOvertime in the tpl object doSaveTemplate builds (mirroring how it already recovers src.bonusType/src.start), set it on the shift objects applyTemplateTap and toggleQuickFillDay construct, and add `isOvertime: t.isOvertime===true` to the templates sanitizeData coercion so it round-trips through storage. If dropping OT from templates is actually intentional, the QUICK ADD/quick-fill chip should say so or omit the OT-looking styling, rather than silently producing a lower number.
